name: Illinois DNR Natural Areas Stewardship Grant
summary: Grants for conservation land trusts to steward Illinois nature preserves and reserves, covering stewardship work, contractors, equipment and staff time, with a small match. The current application deadline is listed as TBD.

eligibility.rule: Be a 501(c)(3) Conservation Land Trust whose purposes include restoration and stewardship of land for conservation
Registered in the State of Illinois Grantee Portal before the deadline
Conduct the project on an Illinois nature preserve, dedicated buffer, or land and water reserve
Have a current approved management schedule and own the site or have an executed owner agreement
Not an NGO whose main purpose is fundraising for local government conservation agencies

documents: Map of each site showing the proposed activities
Approved management schedule for each site
Landowner agreement and notice to the Commission, if not the landowner
IRS determination letter, if new to Illinois state grants in 3 years
Two price quotes for equipment of $5,000 or more

status.quote: Application Deadline: TBD Grant Amount: Up to $100,000 Match: 5% or $1000, whichever is less.

Please submit application materials through the Amplifund portal.

eligibility.quote: Conservation Land Trusts exempt from taxation under Section 501(c)(3) of the federal Internal Revenue Code and include in its purposes the restoration and stewardship of land for conservation purposes.
Applicants must be registered in the State of Illinois Grantee Portal prior to the application deadline date.
All projects must be on eligible lands. This includes Illinois nature preserves, dedicated buffers, and land and water reserves.

Project sites must have a current and approved management schedule and must be owned by the applicant or there must be an executed agreement between the conservation land trust and the property owner.
Non-Governmental Organizations whose primary purpose is to fundraise for local government conservation agencies are not eligible.

documents.quote: The project narrative must be completed and submitted in Amplifund.

Copy of executed agreement between the applicant and the landowner (if applicable) o Copy of notification of executed agreement to Commission (if applicable) o Maps for each site that identify the location of proposed activities o Copy of approved Management Schedule for each site included in the Project Narrative
W-9: All applicants must complete and provide the latest W-9 version as found at www.IRS.gov.

Not-for-profit applicants that have not done business with the State of Illinois in the last 3 years or have reorganized since last doing business with the State must provide a copy of their IRS Determination Letter
Two price quotes for equipment purchase with value of $5,000 or more.

after_award.quote: Quarterly Progress Reports: If the amount of grant funds awarded exceeds $25,000.00, the grantee is required to provide to the DNR quarterly progress reports that describe the progress of the project and expenditures of funds
The grantee shall submit a written Final Report to the department no later than 30 days following the completion of the Project or the ending date of the grant agreement, whichever is earlier
